findings.statement: SCARB1 is a surface protein with a modest ADC suitability score [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.558], but it is enriched in the adrenal gland proteome (tissue-specificity score [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.08]) with high adrenal staining and moderate kidney staining. Only a small share of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1], so on-target off-tumour risk and patchy expression both weigh against a conjugate; a high score would not show a conjugate works.

The cell-type call for SCARB1 does not hold across single-cell datasets: the dominant group is myeloid in Li 2022 but tumour (RCC) in Zhang 2021, with tumour-cell shares of [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336] and [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582]. The top-ranked target may therefore be partly a myeloid signal; only four paired donors back the second dataset.

SCARB1 protein increase replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort, with a log2 fold change of [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334] and adjusted p of [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.28e-10].

CA9 is a known target with a surface call, but the vital-organ proteome shows stomach enrichment (tissue-specificity score [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19]) with high stomach staining, and it was not observed at the cell surface in CSPA. In the weakest quarter of donors few tumour cells express it [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=24.3], so stomach safety and heterogeneity are the open questions.

CA9 was not tested in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort (fewer than ten matched tumour-normal pairs there), so its protein change has no independent replication; this is a gap, not a failure to replicate.

CA9 is flagged as a subgroup target candidate for PBRM1 mutation, with mutant-minus-wild-type log2 difference of [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.971] in CPTAC RNA and [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148] in TCGA RNA. It is not flagged for VHL, BAP1 or SETD2.

CA9 expression is only weakly associated with longer benefit on sunitinib in IMmotion150 (log hazard ratio per SD [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], adjusted p [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.padj=0.332]). The difference between combination and sunitinib is not significant (adjusted p [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.difference_between_arms.padj=0.917]), so CA9 is not a usable treatment-selection biomarker here.

CD70 has the best ADC suitability among the leading candidates [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746], with no vital-organ proteome enrichment (tissue-specificity score [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=0.34]). Staining data are not available, and the weakest-quarter tumour expression is low [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=17.7], so heterogeneity limits any conjugate.

Most CD70 tumour transcripts come from immune cells (share [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654]), and it correlates with CD8 T cells (rho [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_cd8_t_cells=0.278]). This weakens it as a tumour-cell-intrinsic ADC target and suggests an immune-microenvironment role; a negative log hazard ratio on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is reported without adjusted significance.
CD70 was not tested in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort (absent or too sparse there), so its protein change lacks independent replication; this is not a failed replication.

NNMT is assigned to tumour (RCC) cells in both single-cell datasets, with tumour-cell share [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.97] in Li 2022 and [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.948] in Zhang 2021, so the signal is tumour-intrinsic.

NNMT protein increase replicates strongly in the confirmatory cohort, log2 fold change [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776] with adjusted p [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.07e-46]; direction and significance matter more than the fold-change size across technologies.
NNMT is not flagged as a subgroup target candidate for VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2 mutation, and does not define the ccA/ccB split, so it would matter across genetic subgroups rather than for one.

PCK1 loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819], adjusted p [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.53e-27]) and both measured phosphosites replicate too.

PCK1 is lower in ccB than ccA tumours at RNA level (TCGA ccB minus ccA log2 difference [gene=PCK1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-2.581]) but the CPTAC protein difference is not significant, and no mutation subgroup is flagged. It is a loss marker, not a drug target.

HK2 protein increase does not replicate: in the confirmatory cohort the log2 fold change is [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256] with adjusted p [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074], against a discovery log2 fold change of [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_discovery_log2fc=2.106]. A top-ten target candidate rests on discovery data only.

PPP1R1A protein loss is not significant in the confirmatory cohort (adjusted p [gene=PPP1R1A; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.17], few matched pairs), although the direction is the same and one phosphosite replicates. The biomarker case rests on discovery protein and TCGA RNA; FABP6 and DUSP9 were not tested in this cohort.

PSAT1 loss, the top biomarker, replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]), although its one phosphosite significant in discovery does not replicate.

VWF is an endothelial signal, not a tumour-cell one: immune cells contribute little of its tumour transcripts (share [gene=VWF; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.016]) and its tumour-cell share in Li 2022 is [gene=VWF; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.002]. Its tumour rise and prognostic value in the biomarker ranking likely reflect vascularity.

SLC16A3 (MCT4) ranks high for ADC suitability [gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.725] and is expressed in a large share of tumour cells even in the weakest quarter of donors [gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=43.7]. Adrenal staining is high and kidney staining moderate, and it has twelve transmembrane segments with a short extracellular part, which limits antibody access.

SLC16A3 protein increase replicates in the confirmatory cohort (log2 fold change [gene=SLC16A3; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=3.551]) and its single measured phosphosite replicates.

ENPP3, a known conjugate target, has a lower suitability score [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.578] and high staining in normal kidney [gene=ENPP3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; kidney_staining_level=3.0] and duodenum, so on-target kidney toxicity is the main concern despite no vital-organ proteome enrichment. Its protein increase replicates in the confirmatory cohort.

caveats: No gene differs between trial arms after correction in IMmotion150 or CheckMate 025; all treatment findings are associations from single arms of modest size and are leads only.
The ADC score combines topology, staining and expression homogeneity; it does not show that a conjugate or radioligand would work, and CD70 lacks staining data.
Confirmatory replication covers protein only in a different cohort and technology; CA9, CD70, FABP6 and DUSP9 were not tested there, which is a gap and not a failed replication.
Second single-cell dataset has only four paired donors; the SCARB1 myeloid versus tumour discrepancy is unresolved.

PSAT1, ALDH6A1, SLC6A19, SLPI, L1CAM, VWF, PCK1 replicate in direction and significance, but these loss markers are not drug targets. Immune and endothelial genes can differ because of infiltration or vascularity.
Treatment, subtype and immune layers were run only for a subset of candidates because of the tool-call budget.
